title: authoring wizard: add stepwise RAG playbook with execution stubs and typed bindings
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add an interactive 'Authoring Wizard' RAG playbook with light execution stubs, TypeScript bindings, a local devcontainer and a smoke CI workflow. No breaking changes.
description: Context: Engineers and docs users asked for a compact, stepwise authoring experience that teaches RAG authoring idioms while providing runnable stubs. This PR adds a lightweight 'Authoring Wizard' playbook (stepwise scenarios, inline assertions) and a set of small execution stubs and typed bindings so users can run and extend the examples locally. Motivation: accelerate onboarding for new users, provide a reproducible smoke CI path for RAG templates, and surface telemetry probes so platform teams can show realistic traces. What this PR does: - New playbook: examples/authoring-wizard/playbook.yaml with three guided scenarios (index->retrieve->tool-call->finalize). The playbook supports a replay mode for deterministic e2e authoring. - Tool stubs: small TypeScript tool adapters in examples/authoring-wizard/tools/ (http_stub.ts, db_stub.ts, file_tool.ts) showing safe failure modes and structured responses. - Typed bindings: examples/authoring-wizard/bindings.ts with example TypeScript types for tool outputs and tool-caller helpers. - Dev environment: a devcontainer and a small local-runner script so you can run the playbook locally with one command. - Docs: docs/site/rag/authoring-wizard.md with a short tutorial, expected outputs, and troubleshooting tips. - Telemetry probes: examples/authoring-wizard/telemetry/probes.toml that maps probe names used in the playbook to recommended dashboard panels. - CI: ci/workflows/rag-smoke.yml runs a fast smoke invocation of the playbook against the stubs (intended to catch regressions in runtime and example API surfaces). Checklist: - [x] Add playbook and step definitions - [x] Add tool stubs and typed bindings - [x] Add devcontainer & local-runner - [x] Add docs page and code samples - [x] Add smoke CI workflow - [x] Add basic unit/e2e smoke tests Notes on usage: run ./examples/authoring-wizard/local-runner.sh to run all three scenarios and emit a structured trace. The playbook intentionally keeps external I/O minimal so the smoke CI is stable and fast. Related: Linear ENG-7821 tracks follow-ups (editor integration and more assertions). SUP-1187 documents a support case that motivated the improved troubleshooting section. Implementation details and design choices: - Plays are authored as short YAML steps with explicit 'inputs', 'tool_call', and 'assertions' nodes to make expectations machine-checkable. - Tools return structured JSON with an envelope {status, output, diagnostics} so examples can demonstrate graceful degradation. - Typed bindings are intentionally small (50–100 LOC) to act as a template for consuming applications. - Telemetry probes are lightweight tags emitted by the playbook runner; the probes.toml maps to example panels in the docs. Backwards compatibility: nothing in the core API or existing examples is changed; this is additive. Follow-ups: - ENG-7902: integrate the authoring wizard into docs landing page with an interactive iframe. - ENG-7930: add test harness for fuzzing step assertions.
